newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares firm as Creditanstalt recovers.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares firm as Creditanstalt recovers.

text.p: Austrian shares ended with modest gains on Thursday, with sentiment bolstered by firmer European markets and a further recovery in Creditanstalt.
"After a good start the market then fell asleep," said one trader. "We didn't advance further, because selling kept kicking in," said another, in particular citing VA Tech and OMV.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips added on 2.29 points, or 0.22 percent, to 1,042.97 after trading within a tight 1,040.62 to 1,045.53 points. Of its constituents, 10 gained and 11 fell.
"Market conditions are actually good. If we can't confirm 1,040 points and try for 1,050, then the trend will change again," said a trader.

Another said he was pessimistic as the Vienna market was not being propelled higher although the market environment was favourable. "That naturally brings up the question: what happens, when market conditions suddenly turn negative?"
The top gainer was Wolford, up 4.49 percent at 2,790, while VA Tech was the leading decliner, shedding 1.07 percent to close at 1,389.
Creditanstalt's preferred shares were the most actively traded on turnover of 55,580 lots. The shares added on 8.7 schillings to 465.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index inched 0.08 percent higher to 404.89.
The October ATX future advanced two points to 1,047 on turnover of 491 contracts.
